H19 terminal screen for the H89 port (fujinet-5cardstud's src/h89/console.h).
The screen is drawn by cell codes, one byte each: bit 7 is reverse video and
the low seven bits are the H19's own character ROM index (444-29) --
0x00-0x1F the graphics characters, 0x7F the graphics bullet, 0x20-0x7E
ASCII -- the same form the terminal keeps its screen in.
Drawing goes into a back buffer; flush() sends the terminal only the cells
that differ from what it already shows, with as few cursor-address (ESC Y),
reverse-video (ESC p/q) and graphics-mode (ESC F/G) changes as it can, and
erases (ESC K, ESC E) where they are cheaper than spaces. The console runs at
9600 baud, and the shared game code repaints the whole table every poll.
Row 24 is the H19's 25th line, which termInit() turns on for the status bar.

Heathkit H89: the H19 terminal's 80x24, plus its 25th line as row 24
(HEIGHT-1, the status line), which src/h89/console.c turns on.
The board is the 40 column one widened to 80: the score names in full in a
box at columns 11-23, then six player columns eight wide (24-31, 33-40, ...
69-76) between dividers at 23, 32, ... 77. The shared code's three wide
score field sits in the middle of each (SCORE_COL_X), with the score cursor
at its left and the initial over its centre. The dice are 7x3 -- the H19's
cells are about two and a half times as tall as they are wide, so that is
square -- every 9 columns, the roll button under the first player column.
